Consider the circle $S$ and vector field $F$ shown above. Let $C$ be any path where $S$ is traversed once in the **clockwise** direction. Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$

II. ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$

III. ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We now recall the following:

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is true, while statement III is false. Since the force $F$ acts perpendicular to the motion of the particle as it moves around $C,$ it neither helps nor hinders its motion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14152067/assets/c498ddeae8ba4325a4a1dfc0840520c4718bb50a0600970405374dde933e1b1d.png)

So, ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

- Statement II is true. If we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then the situation with regards to the work done by $F$ remains unchanged.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14152067/assets/740429a29b5eb4b72bbfae11e08c9ac272e72e31d395b4dad2602beb4d4ba40a.png)

So, ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
